root.label: Type traits
root.note: Class templates the compiler evaluates to map types to constants or to other types.

children.label: How traits are built
children.note: A primary template gives the default answer and specializations add the exceptions.

children.label: integral_constant
children.note: Holds a static constexpr value; true_type and false_type are its bool instances.

children.label: _t and _v helpers
children.note: Alias templates arrived in C++14 and variable templates in C++17; both are conveniences.

children.label: References are never const
children.note: is_const_v<const int&> is false, and remove_const leaves a reference unchanged.

children.label: Surprising properties
children.note: Several trait names promise more or less than the question they actually ask.

children.label: Trivially copyable
children.note: Asks whether memcpy is valid; a user-provided default constructor does not matter.

children.label: is_trivial
children.note: Also requires trivial default construction; deprecated in C++26.

children.label: is_constructible
children.note: Tests direct-initialization T t(args...), so explicit constructors and narrowing count.

children.label: is_convertible
children.note: Tests copy-initialization through a return statement, so explicit constructors do not count.

children.label: Transformations
children.note: Traits whose result is a type, read through the _t alias.

children.label: decay
children.note: Models pass-by-value: drops references and cv, turns arrays and functions into pointers.

children.label: remove_cvref
children.note: C++20; strips only references and cv, so arrays stay arrays.

children.label: common_type
children.note: Decayed type of the conditional operator; int and unsigned give unsigned.

children.label: Compiler-backed traits
children.note: Questions no specialization can answer are implemented with built-ins.

children.label: Built-in intrinsics
children.note: is_union, is_aggregate, is_final and underlying_type need compiler support.

children.label: Specializing is UB
children.note: Adding specializations of standard traits is undefined behavior unless explicitly permitted.

children.label: Permitted exceptions
children.note: common_type and, since C++20, basic_common_reference may be specialized for program-defined types.

children.label: Unevaluated contexts
children.note: Operands that are type-checked but never executed or odr-used.

children.label: The operators
children.note: sizeof, decltype, noexcept, non-polymorphic typeid and requires expressions.

children.label: std::declval
children.note: Returns add_rvalue_reference_t<T>; odr-using it is ill-formed.

children.label: Control at compile time
children.note: Choosing code paths and combining predicates without unwanted instantiation.

children.label: if constexpr
children.note: C++17; a discarded branch is not instantiated, but only inside a template.

children.label: static_assert(false)
children.note: Fine in a discarded template branch since C++23 (P2593); still fires in non-templates.

children.label: conjunction
children.note: Stops at the first false argument and never instantiates the rest; a fold over ::value does.
